To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the disruption of b2m or the TAP gene in ES cells and the introduction of recipient matched MHC class I gene into the ES DC resulted in the generation of genetically modified DC with the capacity to activate the antigen specific cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTL) without being recognized by the pre activated CTL or priming the CTL against intrinsic HLA class I encoded epitopes.
we have established an effective method to overcome the problem of H 2 mismatch in the future clinical applications of ES DC by modifying the b2m and TAP genes.

the modification of the b 2 microglobulin or TAPI gene in ES cells may be an effective strategy for the genetic modification to overcome the problem of H 2 allele mismatch between ES cells and the recipients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of antigen presenting cells (APC) from embryonic stem (ESC) cells.
the development of a novel method for the genetic manipulation of dendritic cells.
the genetic modification of ES derived DC and the application of the modified ES DC for the activation of antigen specific CTL in vivo.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the b2 microgloblin or TAP1 gene disruption and the subsequent introduction of recipient matched MHC class I gene into ES DC is a promising strategy to generate allogeneic DC for clinical application.

the b2m gene disruption and the introduction of recipient matched Kd gene into ES cells resulted in the generation of genetically modified ES DC that were capable of eliciting antigen specific immunity in vivo.
the introduction of the Kd molecule into b2m+ or TAP1+ ES DC, or the disruption of b2m or the TAP1 gene in ES DC can effectively eliminate the recognition of the ES DC by CTL.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the b2m gene disruption and the introduction of b2m linked Kd gene into ES DC could result in a cell population that could be used for the induction of CTL specific to the introduced Kd allele and could overcome the HLA allele mismatch problem.
b2m /Kd and TAP /Kd ES cells were successfully generated. b2m and TAP disruption did not affect the differentiation of the cells to DC.
the genetic modification of ES cells or iPS cells to DC is feasible, which will be a useful tool for future immunotherapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use genetically modified ES DC to prime CTL against the target cells, irrespective of the H 2 allele mismatch.
the modification of b2m or the TAP gene is effective in overcoming the problem of H2 mismatch in allogeneic stem cell derived dendritic cells.

the modification of the b 2 m or TAP genes in the human ES cells may be a useful strategy to resolve the problems of HLA class 1 allele mismatch between the human ES or induced PSCs and the recipients to whom the cells are to be transplanted.
